sections.sectionSummaryBrief: This section explains the paradoxical unity of the bounded and the boundless in G-d, as expressed in the phrase "there is none like Him," and how this is reflected in creation.

translations.translation: Now we must explain the meaning of "One, there is none like Him"—how could it enter one's mind that there is one like Him, such that it is necessary to say there is none like Him?
The explanation is as follows: It is written,
"And You are He, and Your years will not end."
At first glance, this is not understood: how can "Your years" be said of the Most High, for this implies time and limitation, while the blessed Creator is unbounded?
Moreover, the phrase "Your years will not end" seems to contain a contradiction within itself.
The Rashba, of blessed memory,
explained that because a bounded human being cannot grasp the unbounded, having no mental image at all of the unbounded—
just as we have no image of the non-spatial and the timeless,
even more so, we have no image of the aspect of the limitless—
therefore it says "Your years," which a person can grasp, and then says "will not end," that the years do not cease; in this way it is possible to give a person some intellectual satisfaction.
This is like "to break the ear," similar to "the eyes of G-d," "the ears of G-d,"
"Let Your ear be attentive"
"and Your eyes open," etc.
In Chassidic terms, the matter can be understood through Abba and Imma.

For it is known that time exists in the aspect of Malchut, as it is written, "Your kingdom is a kingdom of all worlds, and Your dominion is in every generation"—past, present, and future belong to the aspect of Malchut: "He reigned, He reigns, He will reign."
This is "the day of the Holy One, blessed be He, is a thousand years,"
for units, tens, and hundreds are in Biyah, and thousands in Atzilut,
and this is in the aspect of Malchut; but above the aspect of Malchut, there is no aspect of time.
Nevertheless, it cannot be said that there is no root and source for the aspect of time there,
for
the Ein Sof, just as He has power in the unbounded, so too does He have power in the bounded.
This is the aspect of the vessels of the Ten Sefiros of Atzilut, which are the first limitation that emanates from Him.

This is the Name Sha-dai, whose root is the aspect of the Reshimu, which is the power of limitation within the Ein Sof, and it is the root and source of the vessels, as explained elsewhere in the discourse "Vayetzavem" of 5567.
But the Name Havayah is "He was, He is, and He will be as one," that is, the aspect of the Ein Sof, the unbounded.
From the aspect of the Name Havayah, the worlds would have been in a state of actual infinity,
and through the Name Sha-dai, who said to His world "enough," the worlds came into being in a state of existence and limitation.
Nevertheless, it is written "Havayah reigns, Havayah reigned, Havayah will reign," for within the limitation of past, present, and future, the aspect of the Ein Sof, the unbounded, shines.
Therefore, the creation that comes from the aspect of Malchut is in a state of boundlessness,

for although the creatures are bounded and should have had limitation in their existence, they are in a state of boundlessness—like the multitude of the inanimate and the vegetative, trees, grasses, fruits, and grain, which are truly without measure,
and this is from the aspect of the Ein Sof, the unbounded, that shines within the aspect of Malchut.
This is "there is none like Him"—the union of two opposites: the boundless and the bounded.
This is like the concept of "impossibilities are nullified in the bosom of the Creator,"
for there are some philosophers who say that impossibilities have a fixed nature, such as "riding and not riding," which is impossible, heaven forbid, even in the bosom of the Creator.
But in truth, it is not so; rather, impossibilities are nullified, and He can be both riding and not riding, even though in our intellect it is not understood how this is.
And we see with our senses the aspect of bounded and boundless together in the multitude of creations, without measure and without end, even though they are bounded.
From this we understand that in the power of the Ein Sof is the ability for two opposites—bounded and boundless—to exist, and likewise riding and not riding.
This is "One, there is none like Him."

sections.sectionSummaryBrief: This section explains that the uniqueness of Israel lies in their power to draw down G-dly revelation through their actions, even beyond the commandments, because their souls are rooted in G-d's very essence.

translations.translation: Now we must explain what is the concept of "One, there is none like Him" in relation to Israel.
The explanation is as follows: Our Rabbis, of blessed memory, said that the Holy One, blessed be He, dons tefillin.
And in the tefillin of the Master of the world, what is written? "And who is like Your people Israel, one nation."
The explanation: "The Holy One, blessed be He, dons tefillin" refers to the aspect of Zeir Anpin,
and "dons tefillin" means the drawing down of mochin to Zeir Anpin.
Now, our Rabbis, of blessed memory, said
on the verse "He declares His words to Yaakov"—that what He does as a mitzvah, He commands Israel to do; meaning that through Israel doing, He does.

For when a Jewish man dons tefillin below, through this the Holy One, blessed be He, dons tefillin—the drawing down of mochin to Zeir Anpin, which are the four sections of tefillin: Kadesh and Vehayah Ki Yevi'acha (Chochmah and Binah), Shema (Da'at), and Vehayah Im Shamoa (Da'at divided into Chessed and Gevurah).

And through his donning tzitzit, through this the Holy One, blessed be He, wraps Himself in tzitzit; and so with all the mitzvos—specifically through the Jewish person performing the mitzvah below, as it were, the Holy One, blessed be He, performs the mitzvah.
This is "and to guard all His commandments"—that they perform and cause His commandments above.
And this is a great praise for Israel, that through the mitzvos they perform, they cause Him, blessed be He, to perform the mitzvos.

The concept of "One, there is none like Him" is as found in the Midrash Rabbah on the verse "Jerusalem has sinned a sin"—do the nations of the world not sin? Rather, the nations of the world are nothing, for their actions do not matter at all.
But Israel, any good thing they do, even if it is not a mitzvah per se, they thereby draw down a drawing of G-dliness, as it is stated in the Zohar
regarding the child who said to them, "I smell from the fragrance of your garments that you have not recited the Shema,"

and this was because they were occupied with the wedding procession, and through this they drew down that same drawing that comes through the Shema—"Havayah our G-d, Havayah is One," which is the unification of Abba and Imma and the unification of Zeir Anpin and Nukvah.
Similarly, through the union of a man and a woman, the union above is effected, as it is said,
"A man and a woman—if they are worthy, the Divine Presence rests between them," and therefore seven blessings are recited over this.
And even in matters that are not a mitzvah at all, if they are done with intention for the sake of Heaven, they thereby draw down a revelation of G-dliness, as when one
puts on shoes and recites the blessing "Who has provided for all my needs,"

for through the wearing of shoes, they draw down the aspect of "How beautiful are your feet in sandals"—that Metatron is called the shoe of the Shechinah, and likewise the sandal, as explained in Likkutei Torah on the discourse "Mah Yafu Pa'amayich," that this is the aspect of the Parsa that separates between Atzilut and Biyah, which covers the foot, the aspect of Malchut, so that the worlds are in a state of limitation, etc.

And "How beautiful are your feet in sandals" means that even in the sandals there should be the beauty of your feet, that there should be the aspect of revelation, and through the sandals it becomes possible to receive,
(similar to "and He guided them in sandals," as explained elsewhere).
Thus, even in matters that are not mitzvos, they draw down a revelation of G-dliness through them.
And this is specifically in Israel, as mentioned above in the name of the Midrash,
and this is "One, there is none like Him."

And all this is because "Havayah has chosen you to be a people for Him," etc., and it is known that this is the essential choice in the souls of Israel, not due to the fulfillment of Torah and mitzvos, as it is written, "Only in your fathers did Havayah delight"
Havayah.

Therefore, they have the power to draw down, through their mitzvos, the aspect of the mitzvos above, and also in every matter they do with intention for the sake of Heaven, even if it is not a mitzvah, they draw down a revelation of G-dliness through it,
for they are "one nation in the land" in matters of the land,
and through a call from the straits of matters of the land, "answer me in the wide expanse of Yah"—the essential expanse of the Ein Sof.

sections.sectionSummaryBrief: This section explains that the love of Israel for G-d cannot be extinguished by any intellectual comprehension or even by the revelations of Gan Eden, because their souls are rooted in G-d's very essence, beyond all grasp.

translations.translation: A)
And this is "Many waters cannot extinguish the love, and rivers will not wash it away."
"Many waters" are contemplation, comprehension, and understanding—
all these cannot extinguish the love and quench the thirst of the souls of Israel for G-dliness,
and "rivers" are the revelations of Gan Eden,
the lower and upper Gan Eden cannot wash it away.
And even when Israel are in a lowly state, "we have a little sister" whose merits are few, and the nations of the world argue that Israel also sin,

nevertheless, even then, through their service in practical mitzvos and in action with simple intention for the sake of Heaven, they reach the aspect of the essential expanse, which is above all revelations,
and therefore contemplation, and even the revelations of Gan Eden, cannot extinguish nor wash away the love of Israel for their blessed Maker, in whom the souls of Israel are rooted,
for "no thought"
can grasp Him at all,
even the primordial thought of Adam Kadmon,
except when it grasps and is clothed in Torah and its mitzvos,
as explained by our master, the Alter Rebbe.

And because of this, even "many waters," which are the nations of the world, and "rivers," which are the kings of the nations and their ministers, cannot wash away the love of the Holy One, blessed be He, for the children of Israel,
as explained in the Targum and the Midrash,
that even though they sin, they are not rebuked,
and the reason is because "Havayah has chosen you"—the essential choice in the souls of Israel,
for they are rooted in the very Essence, which is above even the root of Torah and mitzvos.
Like a little girl who does not do the will of her parents, they do not rebuke her,
because the little girl's essence is rooted in the essence of the father and mother,
in a place where all other matters of the father and mother have no place,
and so too with the souls of Israel, who are rooted in the very Essence, as it were,
and therefore they are not rebuked,
and even those who say, "Let us be"
like the nations, like the families of the lands—behold, thus says my Lord Havayah: "You shall surely not be,"
"if not with a strong hand and an outstretched arm, etc., I will reign over you, and I will bring you into the bond of the covenant, and you shall know that I am Havayah."
And He will give them—this is the Holy One, blessed be He, from the aspect of the essential expanse—all the wealth of His house,
"With wisdom a house is built, and with understanding it is established, and with knowledge the rooms are filled with all precious and pleasant wealth,"
and He will also give them all the spoils and plunder of the war of Gog,
for ours is the victory, speedily in our days, through our righteous Moshiach.
